svg.text: WHAT YOU HAVE TO FEED IT — and the poses are not free

a.data-tip: The real scenes are eight handheld forward-facing captures taken with a cellphone, with 20 to 62 images each and one eighth held out for testing. The synthetic scenes are pathtraced renderings, 100 views in and 200 held out for testing at 800 by 800 pixels.

An open-source structure-from-motion and multi-view stereo package. It matches features across the photographs, then solves jointly for where each camera was, what its intrinsics are and a sparse point cloud. NeRF uses it on the real captures to recover poses, intrinsics and scene bounds.

A set of RGB images, one camera pose and intrinsics per image, and near and far bounds for the scene. On the synthetic data these are exact by construction; on the real captures they are COLMAP estimates, and the paper says so.

A pose error is not noise the optimiser can average away. Two cameras that disagree about where they were disagree about where the surface is, and the only way to satisfy both is to smear the density field. The paper does not measure sensitivity to pose error.
a.text: Just some photos is the wrong takeaway
A pose error is not noise that averages out. Two cameras that disagree about where they stood disagree about where the
surface is, and the only density field that satisfies both is a smeared one. Pose accuracy enters the result as geometry error.
The synthetic results use exact poses; the real ones use COLMAP estimates. But Table 1’s columns are different scenes and
captures, so they cannot isolate pose error; that would need a pose-perturbation study, which the paper lacks.

svg.text: P tens of views, not thousands: 100 for synthetic scenes
A enough overlap for feature matching to succeed
P a static scene: nothing may move between shots
A fixed exposure and white balance
P known near and far bounds for the volume

a.data-tiphead: How far the view count can drop
a.data-tip: Rows 5 and 6 of Table 2 cut the input set. With 50 views quality falls from 31.01 to 29.79, and with 25 it falls to 27.78. The paper notes that its 25-view result still beats the three baselines given 100 views each, citing the supplementary material.
